chapter: Art Hodes, Bechet and Blue Note
title: Playing with Art Hodes at McKinley Hall; the first Blue Note record
summary: He worked club dates at McKinley Hall and recorded St. James Infirmary for Blue Note with Hodes and Max Kaminsky.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I see. Well, when did you start doing some work with Art Hodes -- the piano player Art Hodes?
I worked with Art Hodes... I did a lot at a place called McKinley Hall.
Was the War still going on, or had it...?

Yes. McKinley Hall. That was a... Dancers used it... You know, dancers... They would use five pieces. We didn't stay there a long time. It was just a club date. Like, we'd (?) the night, tomorrow night we might be there, and the next night they had some other band there, you know. That's round about Eleventh Street and Sixth Avenue or Seventh Avenue...

Yeah, something like that. McKinley Hall. Anyway, we recorded... I just remember what year it was. Anyway, we did a recording of "St. James Infirmary," and had the record out on there. Because somehow the group ...(?)... a big hit. We recorded at Blue Note.
These were some things with Art Hodes' Original Trio, with Max Kaminsky on trumpet.
Max Kaminsky, yeah. On Blue Note.
